subject: Data Passport — execution loci, subprocessors, and deletion assurances
messages:
From: Elena Ruiz <elena.ruiz@novamed.com>
To: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.ai>
Cc: procurement@novamed.com
Date: 2026-09-02T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Data passport request: processing footprint and deletion controls

Rafael —

Thanks for the demo yesterday. Novamed is evaluating Redwood for some of our NLP inference needs in clinical triage. Before our security committee meeting next week, they asked for a compact "data passport" that answers a few concrete questions about where requests are executed and how deletion is handled. Can you confirm the following at a high level?

1) Primary execution regions (cloud regions / countries) for hosted API requests and any common failover hops
2) Which subprocessors or cloud providers touch request payloads or ephemeral caches (by region if possible)
3) Retention defaults for request payloads, KV cache, and logging/observability artifacts
4) SLA / timeline when Novamed requests deletion of customer data (including cached KV) — does Redwood support on-demand erasure and what is the expected maximum timeline?
5) Any encryption-in-transit and at-rest specifics we should include in our deck

If you have a short PDF or diagram we can share with the security committee, that would be ideal.

Appreciate it —
Elena
Elena Ruiz
Security Lead, Novamed Health
elena.ruiz@novamed.com

From: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.ai>
To: Elena Ruiz <elena.ruiz@novamed.com>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, connor_obrien@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-09-02T11:30:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Data passport request: processing footprint and deletion controls

Elena —

Thanks for the clear list. I attached a concise Data Passport (redwood_data_passport_v1.pdf) and a simple processing map (redwood_processing_map_v2.csv) that answer each question; below is a short summary you can paste into the committee deck.

1) Execution regions
- Primary hosted API endpoints: us-east-1 (primary), eu-west-1 (regional replica for EU customers).
- Failover/replication: requests will fall back to the nearest available region per routing policy; we maintain compatible model variants in us-east-1, eu-west-1, and asia-southeast1 for APAC customers.

2) Subprocessors / who touches payloads
- Compute: AWS (EC2/GPU in us-east-1, eu-west-1), GCP (T4/TPU pools in asia-southeast1 for APAC), and optionally Azure for Dedicated customers.
- Edge/network: Cloudflare (CDN/edge routing), Fastly for some customers.
- Observability and metrics: Datadog (metrics/traces), Sentry (errors) — these receive metadata and aggregated traces; full request payloads are never sent to observability subprocessors.
- Persistent storage: S3-compatible buckets owned by Redwood or in a customer-owned VPC for Private deployments.

3) Retention defaults
- Request payloads: default ephemeral retention is 30 days for hosted API (configurable by contract), with an optional customer-controlled TTL.
- KV cache (model context caching): short-lived by default (24 hours) and rotated; can be configured longer for Dedicated customers.
- Logs & observability: request metadata/trace logs retained 90 days; aggregated metrics retained longer by plan.

4) Deletion SLA (customer-initiated)
- On-demand erasure supported: developer/tenant deletion API initiates purge of stored payloads and KV cache.
- Typical timeline: 24–72 hours for ephemeral caches and storage objects; up to 30 days for background archival shards to be scrubbed (we provide deletion confirmation receipts).
- Cross-border caches: if data was routed temporarily through another region, deletion removes copies in those regions per the same SLA.

5) Encryption and controls
- In-transit: TLS1.2+ with enforced strong ciphers.
- At-rest: AES-256 for stored blobs and KMS-backed keys.
- Key management: Redwood integrates with customer KMS for Private deployments; hosted customers use Redwood-managed KMS with key separation at tenant level.

Attachments and links included. If Novamed needs, we can produce an EU-only execution profile that pins processing to eu-west-1 and restricts cross-region fallback (this is a Dedicated/Private configuration and requires a short legal/ops attachment).

Next steps:
- I can update the Data Passport with any additional evidence you need (SOC 2 section, network traceroutes, or subprocessors POAs).
- Marissa (cc) is our legal lead and can confirm contractual commitments around residency and deletion timelines.

Best,
Rafael Mendes
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
rafael.mendes@redwood.ai

Attachments: redwood_data_passport_v1.pdf (summary + evidence), redwood_processing_map_v2.csv (region -> subprocessors map)

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Elena Ruiz <elena.ruiz@novamed.com>, Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.ai>
Cc: connor_obrien@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-09-02T13:10:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Data passport request: processing footprint and deletion controls

Elena / Rafael —

Quick legal clarifications to include in the committee notes:

- Legal basis: Redwood processes customer-supplied inference requests as a data processor; legal basis for processing rests with Novamed as controller (we will sign the DPA and add required clauses for EU customers).
- Data residency commitments: For hosted customers, we provide region-targeting controls (you can request EU-only processing). For strict residency requirements, our Private/VPC or Dedicated options are the recommended path and come with contractual residency SLAs.
- Deletion warranties: We provide contractual commitments for deletion with a stated maximum remediation window (typical contract language: Redwood will complete deletion of customer data from production and backups within 30 calendar days from receipt of a validated deletion request). We also provide deletion receipts and logs for your audit.

I'll follow up with a short redlineable DPA excerpt if Novamed wants to propose language. Rafael — happy to get the EU-only profile note you mentioned above so I can map contractual wording to operational controls.

Marissa Cole
Head of Legal Operations, Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.ai

From: Elena Ruiz <elena.ruiz@novamed.com>
To: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.ai>, marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Cc: Carlos Mendez <carlos.mendez@novamed.com>, procurement@novamed.com
Date: 2026-09-03T15:45:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Data passport request: processing footprint and deletion controls

Thanks — this is very helpful. Two quick follow-ups from the security committee:

A) For the EU-only profile you mentioned, can you provide a one-paragraph summary we can add to the slide deck that states: where requests will be executed, which subprocessors are allowed, and the impact on failover (i.e., will failover to US be disabled entirely or limited)?

B) Procurement asked for a short mutual action checklist (named points and owners) and an estimated time to have a contract with residency addendum in place (Novamed expects ~3 weeks for standard review). Can Redwood commit to a timeline for signature and a point of contact?

If you can drop the EU-profile blurb and the MAP (mutual action plan) by EOD tomorrow, we'll include it in our Wednesday packet.

Elena
